title: Deep rock: the colour static
question: Does the rock now read as two kinds of stone meeting, rather than as noise? And is the boundary at the right scale — would you want it looser or tighter?
context_md:
The other half of the deep-rock complaint. Same crop of solid rock, same
seed, nothing else changed.

You saw this alongside the light blocks and I fixed those first because
you named them by name. This is the rest of it.

The rock is meant to change country as you walk — patches of neutral grey
against warm sandstone, with a wandering boundary. That intent was right.
The implementation put the wander in **white noise, one coin flip per
cell**, so instead of a coastline you got the two colours sprayed through
each other everywhere. And because the two families differ in *hue* as
well as brightness, it was a colour dither, which is why an earlier
attempt at this — turning the render's grain down — did nothing you could
see. Measured on this crop: luma speckle down 61%, colour speckle down
82%.

The boundary scale is now a knob and I picked it by eye from three: 14
cells reads as camouflage blotches, 96 as a bare sweeping curve, 40 as a
coastline with bays and peninsulas. It ships at 40. Say if you want it
looser or tighter.

Two things worth knowing:

- Every world's colouring changes with this. It is a shift, not a wipe —
  all four rock families are still present in every preset, in similar
  proportions.
- There is still fine speckle inside each country. That is a separate,
  much smaller rule ("12% of cells jump a tone", brightness only, no hue),
  and to my eye it now reads as rock texture rather than noise. I left it
  rather than change two things at once. If it still looks like static to
  you, it is a one-line follow-up.
